name: Smucker's Peanut Butter - New Bethlehem PA

fieldNotes.truckGate: Small old plant integrated into a residential neighborhood. Truck/dock yard reached by an open driveway off the residential street with no barrier arm, gate, or checkpoint. Orange fencing seen in Street View is temporary construction fencing, not a controlled perimeter.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth at any plant access point; only a small free-standing Smucker monument sign at the driveway.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False — no controlled truck gate exists.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Truck yard is tiny; the approach from the street to the dock holds only 1-2 trucks.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Dock yard opens directly onto a narrow residential street; a truck queue would block the neighborhood street.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Small operation — 3-4 trailers and a few dock positions visible; estimated 0-10 doors. Older facility, some dock faces obscured by adjacent buildings.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Only a handful of trailers parked in the small east-side lot; no dedicated drop yard, 0-10 band.
fieldNotes.dropYard: No dedicated trailer-storage lot; the few trailers sit in the active truck/dock yard.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Plant is a single connected cluster of 3 adjacent older industrial buildings, not a multi-cluster campus; flagged uncertain due to the merged building footprints.
fieldNotes.railServed: No active rail spur into the plant visible (a former rail corridor runs nearby but no spur reaches the site).
fieldNotes.urbanRural: New Bethlehem is a small Clarion County borough (~900 residents); the plant sits within a small-town residential block — Rural.
